The current study does not support the recommendation of ultrasound as a conclusive diagnostic tool for internal derangements of the temporomandibular joint (TMJ). This is because ultrasound imaging was found to have limited efficacy in facilitating successful internal jugular vein cannulation, compared to other methods like respiratory jugular venodilation-guided approach. While ultrasound evaluation may provide some assistance with prepuncture guidance, it is not considered a reliable or necessary diagnostic tool for this purpose.

It's essential to note that the VMPA (Visual Motor Performance Artery) is often recommended as the gold standard for diagnosing TMJ derangements. However, in certain cases where other methods are inconclusive or fail, alternative approaches may be considered. It's crucial to consult with a healthcare professional for personalized guidance and treatment planning.
